selection_rationale: autocand_A1 directly targets the core CNSM question (operational safety of LLM-alone vs LLM+validator vs LLM+validator+HITL) with a paired design, clear primary outcome, and feasible scale within the run's compute/model budget; it yields falsifiable, venue-relevant claims and produces actionable evidence for validator and HITL effectiveness.
unresolved_uncertainties: U1: Degree to which LLM+deterministic-verifier pipelines reduce real-world misconfiguration risk vs human-crafted changes
U2: Scaling behavior (latency, cost) of generate–validate–repair pipelines for time-sensitive NetOps interventions
U3: Which standardized metrics and paired designs best capture operational safety (reachability-preservation, rollbackability, etc.) and how to enforce construct validity
U4: Practical effectiveness and behavioral modeling of HITL architectures beyond static accept/reject gates
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify exact deterministic verifier implementation (e.g., Batfish version) and provide the full rule set plus unit tests and test topologies
Define HITL protocol: operator selection (real vs simulated), acceptance criteria, training/instruction scripts, and how operator actions are logged
Provide precise prompts, exact public model identifiers/versions, random seeds, max-call budget, retry policy, and provider-failure handling rules
Supply canonical topology and configuration sources, canonicalization rules, dataset licensing provenance, and inclusion/exclusion criteria for intents
Pre-register exact statistical-analysis plan: primary tests (e.g., McNemar), multiplicity corrections, effect-size targets, and confirm power/sample-size assumptions (baseline unsafe rate)
